note: P4334 (Pro 28:24) — who robs his father and says 'no transgression' is companion to a destroyer.

dims.v: self-justifying sin — robbing a parent and denying it is wrong
the transgression of robbing father or mother while saying 'that is no transgression' — sin excused and rationalised, the self-justification that makes a plunderer of his own parents feel innocent
the destroyer he is kin to (266660)
welded to the destructiveness his excuse makes him share

pesha (transgression) — 'whoever robs his father or mother and says, 'that is no TRANSGRESSION''; to sin and rationalise it away is doubly evil. Self-justification hardens a plunderer into a destroyer (cf 30:11-14).
destructiveness — the ruin-worker whose companion the self-excusing robber is
the destroyer/ruiner to whom the one who robs his parents and excuses it is a companion — the destructive nature that self-justified plundering makes a man share
the self-excused sin that joins him to it (266657)
welded to the rationalised robbery that makes him kin to ruin
shachath (destroy/ruin) — 'is a companion to a man who DESTROYS'; the self-excusing robber of his parents is kin to the wanton destroyer. To rationalise plunder is to join the ranks of the ruinous.
